environment.description: Same application container deployed on EKS (Kubernetes 1.28) with the following pod-level controls: (1) Pod Security Admission enforced at 'restricted' profile on the namespace, which mandates non-root UID, drops ALL capabilities, sets readOnlyRootFilesystem, and disallows privilege escalation. (2) A custom seccomp profile loaded via the node's /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/report-svc.json that uses SCMP_ACT_ERRNO for the execve, execveat, and forkexec syscall families (effectively blocking subprocess.run and any child process creation). (3) The container's filesystem is read-only (readOnlyRootFilesystem: true) with only an emptyDir volume mounted at /var/lib/reports with a 50Mi sizeLimit. The combination means: even if the attacker crafts a malicious max_age_days payload for command injection, the seccomp profile blocks execve/execveat at the kernel level, returning EPERM before any shell or child process can spawn.
